# Template: did_trends
The difference-in-differences picture: treated and control group outcome lines over time moving in parallel before a policy, a dashed vertical line at the policy date, the treated line diverging afterwards, a dashed counterfactual continuing the parallel path, and an effect arrow between counterfactual and actual at the end. Choose this scene for ANY request about difference-in-differences, DiD, parallel trends, treated vs control groups over time, policy evaluation with before/after comparison, or counterfactual outcome paths. This is a SCHEMATIC — the two paths are drawn from shape knobs, not from a data series — but `effect` and `treat_at` take a code element's variable via a "{id.var}" token, so the divergence can be the coefficient a regression in Python actually estimated. A token must arrive already on THIS figure's scale: `effect` is CLAMPED to -4..4 and `treat_at` to 2..8, silently, so have the script rescale first (an effect in dollars or log-odds must be divided down to the schematic's units) — an unscaled estimate pins to the edge, or reads as flat, and draws a confident-looking figure that is wrong. TYPE the `group_labels` by hand; until the script has run the figure draws its default schematic, so every beat already exists.
Parameter schema:
{
 "type": "object",
 "properties": {
  "effect": {
   "oneOf": [
    {
     "type": "number",
     "description": "Divergence between treated and counterfactual at the end, -4..4 (default 1.8)."
    },
    {
     "type": "string",
     "pattern": "^\\{[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*\\.[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.]*\\}$"
    }
   ]
  },
  "treat_at": {
   "oneOf": [
    {
     "type": "number",
     "description": "Policy time on the 0-10 axis, 2-8 (default 5)."
    },
    {
     "type": "string",
     "pattern": "^\\{[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*\\.[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.]*\\}$"
    }
   ]
  },
  "group_labels": {
   "oneOf": [
    {
     "type": "array",
     "minItems": 2,
     "maxItems": 2,
     "items": {
      "type": "string"
     },
     "description": "Names for [treated, control] (default [\"Treated\", \"Control\"])."
    },
    {
     "type": "string",
     "pattern": "^\\{[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*\\.[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.]*\\}$"
    }
   ]
  },
  "show_counterfactual": {
   "type": "boolean",
   "description": "Dashed continuation of the treated group's parallel path (default true)."
  },
  "y_label": {
   "type": "string",
   "description": "Default \"Outcome\"."
  },
  "title": {
   "type": "string"
  }
 }
}
Element ids your commands can reference:
- axes: the coordinate axes (a group with captions)
- control_line: the control group's line with its end label
- treated_line: the treated group's line with its end label
- treat_line: dashed vertical line at the policy date (with caption)
- counterfactual: the dashed counterfactual path with its end label (when show_counterfactual)
- effect_arrow: double arrow between counterfactual and actual at the end, with caption
- title: figure title, when set
Examples:
Request: "Draw a difference-in-differences chart with parallel pre-trends." → params: {"title":"Difference-in-differences"}
Request: "Show a DiD where the policy HURT the treated group." → params: {"effect":-1.5,"title":"A harmful policy"}

In YAML: `template: did_trends` and `params:` per the schema above; commands name the element ids above.
